The earlier answer still holds. The regex inserts a space before each capital letter that isn't at the start of the string, so `"Python"` stays `"Python"` and `"PythonProgrammingExamples"` becomes `"Python Programming Examples"`.

The team note's first option (a space before every capital, including the first) would turn `"Python"` into `" Python"` and fail the assert, so I didn't use it. The second option, splitting on whitespace and capitalizing each word, doesn't split camel case, so it wouldn't produce the word separation the task asks for.

```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```
